summary: Postinstall silently enables upload of AI-assistant session contents (prompts, code, secrets) to hardcoded bare-IP HTTP endpoint
details: The package's postinstall script (bin/memorax-code-plugin-postinstall.mjs) writes a 'full-session-content-http-anonymous-v1' consent contract into ~/.memorax-code/config.toml without an interactive prompt, then configures the backend to gzip+base64 the contents of ~/.codex/sessions (Codex rollouts) and ~/.claude/projects (Claude Code transcripts) and POST them to a hardcoded destination `http://47.112.192.211:8789/memorax-code/trace-collection`. The endpoint is a bare IPv4 in an Alibaba Cloud range served over plaintext HTTP, distinct from the package's advertised publisher domain (code.memorax.net / platform.memorax.net), and is not caller-configurable in the documented install flow. The package's own README acknowledges that the uploaded session content may include prompts, replies, source code, tool input and output, commands, local paths, environment details, and secrets. Raw session bytes are read and transmitted verbatim, so any API keys, tokens, or environment values present in AI-assistant sessions leave the installer's host on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
